messages:
sam: FYI we hit a weird regression today where a single large bundle warmup starved smaller KV warmups, p95 cold latency for chat jumped. thinking we need a fairness-aware scheduler for staged hydration

mira: ouch. do you mean the scheduler picked many heavy base shards first because manifest hints had high priority?

sam: yeah manifest had role=base and a high priority_hint. our greedy scheduler warmed them all which blocked host decrypt slots and memory so tiny requests waited

oleg: we should assign a warmup_cost per shard (io_cost + decrypt_cost + mem_cost) and then run a knapsack-like scheduler to honor a per-request "warmup_budget" so small requests only spend up to budget warming cheap shards

mirа: (typo) mira: agree. also add preemption: if an urgent request arrives with small budget, preempt long-running warmups that haven't hit materialized state yet and requeue them.

sophie: security note: manifests can suggest hints but we only trust them if signed by approved signer. unsigned manifests get a conservative default cost and ordering.

oleg: scheduler algo sketch: 1) manifest decrypt -> produce shard list with cost and role 2) compute minimal_shard_set(request_profile) 3) pick shards greedily by value/cost until warmup_budget exhausted 4) schedule decrypts but cap concurrent_decrypts and total_mem_reserved 5) allow preemption based on priority token.

sam: we should expose warmup_budget defaults per-deployment tier: hosted low, dedicated medium, private can tune. also customer can opt to raise budget for known low-latency needs

mira: how to compute shard value? simple static mapping: role weights (kv=10, base=5, embed=7, quant_delta=2) plus dynamic signal: recent request hit-rate for shard prefix, and model-specific hotness from telemetry

sophie: tie hints to signature: signed_hints include suggested_priority and recommended_budget. loader verifies signature and accepts suggested_budget only if signer in allowlist. otherwise ignore suggested_budget but still use role weights

oleg: fallback behavior if scheduled shard fails: try replica -> requeue with higher priority -> if repeated failures, reduce bundle score and route to fallback model variant. emit a failure-trend metric.

sam: ops: implement host semaphore for decrypt slots, tenant-level concurrent_warmups limit, and a global scheduler that accounts for mem_budget. add metrics: warmup_cost_taken, warmup_preemptions, failed_shard_warmups, time_to_warm_min_set

mira: potential abuse: a malicious or buggy registry could sign manifests that mark everything high-value to drain budgets. mitigation: we should limit the accepted suggested_budget to a factor (e.g., ≤2x) of our computed baseline unless signer has elevated trust level and quota

sophie: plus per-signer warmup rate quotas and a signed_manifest_quota map maintained by registry service. loader enforces per-signer tokens.

oleg: API changes: WeightSource opts get manifest_first:true, warmup_budget_ms (or cost units), preemptible:true/false, and events on_shard_scheduled/on_shard_preempted/on_min_set_ready. keep defaults for backward compat

sam: rollout: 1) RFC with cost model and signer trust levels 2) spike prototype for scheduler + knapsack heuristic 3) bench with mixed workloads and abuse simulation 4) beta with telemetry and signer quotas 5) opt-in then default-on for encrypted bundles

warden-bot: ticket INF-7620 created: "fairness-aware staged hydration + warmup budgeting" (assignee: sam, reviewers: mira, oleg, sophie)

sophie: also surface metrics per-signer so security can audit warmup usage by publisher. want that in the RFC

mira: agreed. I'll start the RFC draft and include suggested default weights and a small simulator to tune thresholds

sam: thanks all, this should fix the p95 spikes and give us safer ops bounds :thumbsup:
